history.summary: The Someshwar Nath Dham at Areraj, ~30 km from Motihari in East Champaran district near the Nepal border, is one of Bihar's most-visited Shiva shrines. Per the Bihar tourism department and Shiva Purana tradition, King Som built the 55-ft-high temple about 2,000 years ago; its five-faced (Panchmukhi) lingam of Mahadeo is believed self-existent (swayambhu). Local lore (per a recent devotional documentary, unverified by ASI) also links Lord Rama's visit and the nearby 36.5-ft Lauriya Areraj Ashokan pillar (c. 249 BCE) to the site. The Shrawani Mela in July-August draws lakhs of pilgrims from Bihar and Nepal; over 200,000 devotees performed jalabhishek on New Year's Day 2025 (Patna Press). NOTE: CSV town 'Motihari' is the district HQ ~30 km away; the temple is in Areraj town (correct town given). The ~2,000-year age claim is traditional, not archaeologically verified.

name: Someshwar Nath Mahadev Temple
town_description: Areraj is a small town in East Champaran district, Bihar, about 30 km from Motihari near the Nepal border; besides the Someshwar Nath temple it is known for the nearby Lauriya Areraj Ashokan pillar.

travel.airport: Jay Prakash Narayan International Airport, Patna (~165 km); the nearest airport with regular service.
travel.railway: Bapudham Motihari station; Areraj is reached by auto-rickshaw/local bus from Motihari (~30 km).
travel.road: About 30 km from Motihari by road (auto-rickshaws and local buses).

visitor_information.best_time: September to April (per Bihar tourism); Shrawani Mela (July-August) and Mahashivratri draw the largest crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published; gates opened early for devotees on festival/New Year days (verify).
